title: The Forty-Eight-Hour Walk
summary: Carrie gets Bjorn and Gunnar to the bank before the account deadline, but the real pressure is that every ordinary household need now depends on money the Vikings still cannot use.
settingText: Busy NYC sidewalk approaching the bank

panelPlan.location: Busy NYC sidewalk approaching the bank
panelPlan.action: Carrie moves fast down a crowded sidewalk with a DTI folder; Bjorn and Gunnar keep pace.

panelPlan.location: Busy NYC sidewalk approaching the bank
panelPlan.action: Bjorn carries the small wrapped hacksilver pouch he still considers real money.

panelPlan.location: Busy NYC sidewalk approaching the bank
panelPlan.action: Gunnar checks the bank address against the route he learned in Issue 3.

panelPlan.location: Busy NYC sidewalk approaching the bank
panelPlan.action: Carrie glances at him.

panelPlan.location: Busy NYC sidewalk approaching the bank
panelPlan.action: They reach the glass-fronted bank.

dialogueInline.text: Forty-eight hours. No account, no rent setup. No rent setup, housing starts yelling at me.
Then we claim the hoard before sunset.
That sentence is doing a lot for my blood pressure.

title: A Retail Fortress
summary: Bjorn's expectation of a defended treasury collides with an ordinary branch full of customers, while Carrie tries to keep the appointment socially normal.
settingText: Outside and inside ordinary bank branch

panelPlan.location: Outside and inside ordinary bank branch
panelPlan.action: Ordinary glass-fronted bank branch with ATM vestibule, queue ropes and fluorescent lobby.

panelPlan.location: Outside and inside ordinary bank branch
panelPlan.action: Gary, the security guard, helps an older customer with the ATM before noticing the trio.

panelPlan.location: Outside and inside ordinary bank branch
panelPlan.action: Bjorn studies Gary's knee brace and relaxed posture.

panelPlan.location: Outside and inside ordinary bank branch
panelPlan.action: Gary looks down at the brace.

panelPlan.location: Outside and inside ordinary bank branch
panelPlan.action: Carrie steers Bjorn toward the teller line.

dialogueInline.text: Great. We are bonding. Keep moving.

title: The Teller
summary: Kevin begins the account as an ordinary service interaction, and Bjorn's age becomes briefly strange without turning the whole scene into spectacle.

panelPlan.action: Kevin receives the DTI identity packet across the teller desk.
He reaches the birth-date field and stops.
Carrie does not look up from her folder.
Bjorn waits with grave patience.
Kevin decides not to engage and keeps processing.

dialogueInline.text: Government ID, tax substitute, address verification.
He was born in eight seventy-nine?

title: Address Is a Place
summary: A proof-of-address requirement exposes the gap between actually living somewhere and being legible to a financial institution, but Carrie solves it without turning the whole issue into a paperwork campaign.

panelPlan.action: Kevin turns one screen toward Carrie.
Carrie places the DTI placement letter and provisional housing confirmation beside the screen.
Kevin points to the required document field rather than arguing.
Gunnar looks from the letter to the teller window.
Carrie asks for the branch manager.

dialogueInline.text: I still need proof of address.
He lives there. DTI placed him there. Here is the letter saying he lives there.
The system needs one document it recognizes.
The house knows us. The bank does not.
Then let's make the bank catch up.

title: Worthy Silver
summary: Bjorn offers hacksilver as a sincere opening deposit and learns that modern money can reject valuable metal while still accepting a number backed by institutional recognition.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn unwraps a small piece of hacksilver and places it carefully on the counter.
Kevin looks at it without touching it.
Bjorn looks genuinely offended, not confused.
Gunnar turns the hacksilver in his fingers after Kevin slides it back.
Carrie looks at Gunnar.

dialogueInline.text: We cannot deposit that as currency.
Yes. It is just not dollars.

title: Carrie's Fifty
summary: Carrie supplies the minimum cash deposit, and Bjorn only accepts once the money is named as debt rather than charity.

panelPlan.action: Carrie places fifty dollars on the counter.
Kevin looks between the cash and Carrie.
Bjorn does not let Carrie answer for him.
Carrie meets his eyes.
Bjorn nods once.

dialogueInline.text: Good. It is an advance. You owe me fifty dollars after rent and food.
Name the debt and it can be carried.

title: The Account
summary: Henderson accepts the DTI housing record, opens the account, and gives Bjorn the debit card; the institutional problem is resolved by the end of the first act.

panelPlan.action: Henderson reviews the DTI placement letter and Kevin's screen at a small manager desk.
Carrie pushes the file back into order.
Kevin activates a blue debit card and slides it toward Bjorn.
Bjorn turns the card over.
Henderson answers plainly.
Bjorn looks at Carrie.

dialogueInline.text: This is enough for address verification under the alternative-document policy.
Fifty dollars exists as a balance the bank records and guarantees.

title: A Thing That Exists
summary: Because Bjorn distrusts an account that exists only as recorded value, Henderson gives him the branch's absurd promotional toaster, accidentally providing the tangible acknowledgment he wanted.
settingText: Bank manager desk and supply alcove

panelPlan.location: Bank manager desk and supply alcove
panelPlan.action: Bjorn puts the card down rather than pocketing it.

panelPlan.location: Bank manager desk and supply alcove
panelPlan.action: Henderson gestures toward a stack of new-account promotional boxes.

panelPlan.location: Bank manager desk and supply alcove
panelPlan.action: A plain metal toaster comes out of the box.

panelPlan.location: Bank manager desk and supply alcove
panelPlan.action: Gunnar studies it.

panelPlan.location: Bank manager desk and supply alcove
panelPlan.action: Carrie looks at Henderson.

panelPlan.location: Bank manager desk and supply alcove
panelPlan.action: Bjorn lifts the box with solemn approval.

dialogueInline.text: A pact with no object is wind.
We do still have the account promotion.
He does not qualify for direct deposit.

title: Outside With Too Much Iron
summary: The bank story ends; Bjorn immediately tries to settle Carrie's debt, and she forces him to think about money as household capacity rather than honor resolved in one gesture.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn exits carrying the toaster box under one arm, debit card in the other hand.
He offers the debit card to Carrie.
Bjorn does not lower his hand.
Gunnar looks at the card.
Carrie points toward home.

dialogueInline.text: Yes. And rent is yours. Food is yours. Soap is yours. Being alive is annoyingly expensive.
Then the fifty has other work before it returns.

title: What Is Needed
summary: The toaster arrives home as an odd object, but the real turn is the household making its first shared spending list and revealing separate practical wants.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn sets the boxed toaster on the table. Astrid and the two male Kin gather around while Gunnar removes the packaging.
Astrid examines the toaster slots, then points to a torn seam in her clothing.
First Male Kin lifts the nearly empty detergent sample from the DTI starter bag.
Second Male Kin points to the last piece of fruit from the bodega.
Carrie lays rent estimate and blank paper beside the toaster.
Bjorn puts the debit card in the center of the table.

dialogueInline.text: Good. Rent, food, laundry, household stuff. Then the fire-box.
Then decide what the hoard is for.

title: The Tally
summary: Gunnar turns the account into a finite household tally, and Bjorn sees that modern money is useful precisely because spending it forces choices among real obligations.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar writes simple categories with numbers: RENT, FOOD, SOAP, CARRIE 50.
Bjorn points to Carrie's line.
Carrie moves the rent line above it.
Bjorn resists, then looks at the people around the table.
Bjorn lets the rent line remain on top.

dialogueInline.text: No. Keeping the apartment is first.
A man should repay what he owes.

title: Different Wants
summary: The household narrows the shopping trip together, preserving group continuity while making individual preference visible before anyone begins independent neighborhood routines.

panelPlan.action: Astrid, First Male Kin and Second Male Kin remain together at the table with the shopping list between them.
Astrid crosses out a larger sewing kit and leaves only needles and thread.
First Male Kin chooses laundry soap over a second food item.
Second Male Kin keeps one inexpensive packaged sweet or fruit on the list after Bjorn glances at it.
Bjorn nods rather than removing it.

title: Back to the Bodega
summary: The entire household returns to the store together, and the owner recognizes them enough to treat their financial milestone as ordinary shopping rather than an event.

panelPlan.action: All five displaced adults enter with Carrie. The Bodega Owner recognizes the group from their first night.
Bjorn holds up the debit card.
Astrid and the two male Kin move together through the aisles choosing the specific items from the household list.
Gunnar checks prices against the tally instead of mapping the room.
Carrie watches Bjorn allow other people to put things in the basket without asking permission first.

title: Prices Have Meaning
summary: The finite balance turns abstract value into household choices, but the emphasis stays on what each person chooses rather than on explaining retail systems.

panelPlan.action: Astrid finds needles and thread; First Male Kin lifts laundry soap; Second Male Kin adds one inexpensive snack or fruit.
Gunnar looks at the total of the price tags and then at the tally paper.
Bjorn puts back one larger package of meat without ceremony.
The owner notices.
The owner shrugs and keeps ringing items.

dialogueInline.text: That one is cheaper by weight.

title: First Purchase
summary: Bjorn uses the debit card for the household's first ordinary purchase, making the account real through groceries and chosen objects rather than bank explanation.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn taps or inserts the debit card at the ordinary terminal.
The owner points to the PIN pad.
Carrie turns away enough to give privacy.
The transaction approves.
The owner bags groceries, sewing supplies, laundry soap and the one small extra.

dialogueInline.text: Pick something you will remember. Do not tell me.

title: Coffee Is Not Debt
summary: Bjorn's first discretionary purchase is coffee for Carrie, and he explicitly separates reciprocal affection from the debt he still intends to repay.
settingText: Street coffee cart on the walk home

panelPlan.location: Street coffee cart on the walk home
panelPlan.action: The group stops at an ordinary street coffee cart; Astrid and the two male Kin remain together with the grocery bags.

panelPlan.location: Street coffee cart on the walk home
panelPlan.action: Bjorn points to Carrie's usual order after hearing her say it once.

panelPlan.location: Street coffee cart on the walk home
panelPlan.action: Bjorn pays with the debit card himself.

panelPlan.location: Street coffee cart on the walk home
panelPlan.action: He hands Carrie the coffee.

panelPlan.location: Street coffee cart on the walk home
panelPlan.action: Carrie accepts that distinction.

dialogueInline.text: Is this part of the fifty?

title: The Things Money Became
summary: Back home, the purchases immediately become capability and the promotional toaster becomes useful, letting individual household behavior replace abstract discussion of value.

panelPlan.action: Groceries, sewing supplies, laundry soap and the small extra spread across the table while the toaster sits plugged in safely.
Astrid threads a needle and begins repairing the torn seam.
First Male Kin portions laundry soap while Second Male Kin opens the one small item he chose.
Gunnar lowers two pieces of bread into the toaster.
Toast pops up.
Bjorn looks from the debit card to the repaired clothing, soap, food and toast.

dialogueInline.text: The bank has one useful custom.

title: Debt Named Properly
summary: Bjorn records Carrie's fifty beneath rent rather than trying to erase the debt immediately, turning his honor code into a household plan instead of a crisis.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar's tally now includes the actual grocery spend and remaining balance.
Bjorn draws a firm line beneath CARRIE 50.
Carrie drinks the coffee he bought her.
Bjorn taps the rent line above it.
Bjorn almost objects to the word, then lets it go.

dialogueInline.text: That is the correct dishonor hierarchy.

title: The Neighbor's Snack
summary: A tiny exchange with the Upstairs Neighbor turns one purchased item into relationship, continuing the building thread without making neighborhood integration a formal lesson.

panelPlan.action: Astrid and the two male Kin step into the hallway together to carry household trash to the proper area; the Upstairs Neighbor opens her door.
The neighbor notices the small packaged sweet in Astrid's hand.
Astrid offers one unopened piece from the household bag.
The neighbor accepts and points toward the trash/recycling routine.
Bjorn watches from the doorway as the exchange happens without Carrie mediating.

dialogueInline.speaker: UPSTAIRS NEIGHBOR
dialogueInline.text: Bins are down. Recycling is blue.

title: Silas Has an Angle
summary: Silas tries to turn the toaster and new account into content, but the household's ordinary use of both makes the pitch collapse before Carrie has to fight him.

panelPlan.action: Silas appears at the open doorway with phone half-raised while the toaster is visible on the counter.
Bjorn holds up a piece of toast.
Gunnar keeps eating and does not look at the phone.
Silas lowers the device a few inches.
Carrie walks past him into the room with her coffee.

dialogueInline.text: Okay, Viking toaster unboxing is objectively—
When you say it like that, it loses something.

title: The Household Ledger
summary: Gunnar expands the tally into a recurring household ledger for rent, food and obligations, making financial participation part of the group's shared life rather than Bjorn's private bank problem.

panelPlan.action: The household sits or stands around the table while Gunnar rewrites the tally cleanly.
Simple lines: RENT, FOOD, LAUNDRY, CARRIE 50, REMAINING.
First Male Kin points to laundry; Astrid points to food; Second Male Kin points to remaining money.
Bjorn looks at Gunnar.
The ledger stays on the table where everyone can see it.

dialogueInline.text: You made a map of money.

title: First Toast
summary: The account's first day ends in a shared meal made from purchased groceries and a ridiculous bank toaster, with Carrie sitting inside the household rather than managing it from the edge.

panelPlan.action: Toast, simple food and coffee are distributed around the small table and room.
Carrie remains seated instead of packing up immediately.
Astrid places another piece of toast near her before turning back to the meal.
Carrie looks at the toast, then stays.
The household eats without anyone explaining the account.

title: What the Hoard Is For
summary: Bjorn concludes that the account matters because it can preserve obligations and support people, not because the bank convinced him recorded numbers are inherently real.

panelPlan.action: Debit card, bodega receipt, household ledger and brass key sit near one another on the table.
Bjorn looks at the objects, then at the room around them.
Gunnar looks at groceries, soap and repaired clothing.
Astrid and the two male Kin continue separate evening tasks.
Bjorn folds the card into a safe place rather than displaying it.

dialogueInline.text: The card is not the hoard.
No. It is a road to it.

title: The Tally of Dishonor
summary: The issue closes with the unfinished household ledger visible beside everything the account enabled; Bjorn accepts that carrying a named, planned debt over time is compatible with honor.

panelPlan.action: Carrie stands near the door while the ledger, debit card, brass key, bodega receipt and toaster remain visible in the lived-in room.
Astrid finishes the repair she began; First Male Kin puts laundry soap away; Second Male Kin saves part of his small extra for later.
Bjorn points to the CARRIE 50 line rather than crossing it out.
Gunnar leaves the tally open where everyone can see it.
After Carrie leaves, the household settles normally despite the unpaid line.
Bjorn looks from the tally to the household.

dialogueInline.text: Rent first. Then groceries. Then me.
Then it is not dishonor yet.
